page: Amazon Web Services r7iz.metal-16xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server offering dedicated, non-virtualized access to 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6455B processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, it features an x86_64 architecture backed by 60 MB of L3 cache, Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), and AVX-512 vector support. The system is equipped with 512 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. It does not include integrated local storage or dedicated graphics accelerators, relying on remote network-attached block storage and offering a 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark evaluations place this instance in upper performance tiers across compute and in-memory operations. In Geekbench testing, the server achieved top-decile ratings for both single-core (2,285.0) and multi-core (22,751.0) execution, complemented by strong PassMark CPU scores exceeding 80,000. In-memory throughput is reinforced by PassMark database operation scores in the top 10% and Redis SET performance reaching 85.67 million operations per second. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate substantial throughput, hitting 244.66 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 5,705.78 GB/sec on cached small-block reads.

From a resource utilization standpoint, the bare-metal architecture removes hypervisor virtualization tax, yielding predictable low latency and full hardware instruction set access. However, architectural tradeoffs exist: the complete absence of onboard NVMe storage necessitates reliance on network storage for persistence, and the lack of GPUs caps large-scale neural network generation speeds to moderate levels. For CPU-bound vector acceleration, integrated AMX instructions partially offset the absence of discrete accelerators.

Amazon Web Services r7iz.metal-16xl is well suited for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, including large in-memory databases, electronic design automation (EDA), relational database management systems requiring heavy caching, and latency-sensitive transaction processing.

It delivers 512 GB of DDR5 system memory at 5 GHz, translating to 8 GB per vCPU, without onboard local disk storage or discrete GPUs. Network throughput is rated at 25 Gbps baseline. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate exceptional compute and caching capabilities, with Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores landing in the top 10%, alongside high database throughput exceeding 85 million Redis SET operations per second. Hardware-level acceleration includes AVX-512 and AMX instructions. The lack of local storage requires external network storage volumes, while the unvirtualized configuration delivers low-latency processing ideal for large in-memory databases, real-time analytics, and enterprise relational workloads.
